item.title: Digital Engagement Officer
item.description: Compass is looking to recruit a Digital Engagement Officer as we enter an exciting new period for progressive politics in the UK. The Digital Engagement Officer will lead on writing copy for our digital comms, focusing on our member and supporter mailings, website and social media, and manage our mailing list and inboxes. We’re looking for someone with experience of managing mailing lists and writing copy for a variety of audiences and actions. You should have experience crafting digital communications that motivate people to take action, and be excited about creating journeys over time that integrate the threads of our fundraising, national campaigns, local organising and ideas output together into the story of Compass. You should have a background in digital engagement, specifically in direct marketing through mailings or copywriting for fundraising and campaigning, ideally with a familiarity with CRM software and GDPR regulations. You should be a self-starter, with a proven ability to self-organise and comfortable working in a small, dynamic team. You should have a keen understanding of the political landscape in which Compass operates and be interested in progressive political ideas and working in a pluralist way to make change happen. This role involves: Writing copy for mailings, blogs, website content and social media that is compelling, accessible, imaginative and aligned with Compass’s tone of voice and core script. Writing and editing with various actions in mind, including event invitations, fundraising asks and campaigns. Proofreading mailings, publications, funding bids. Developing our voice and core scripts, particularly around specific campaigns or fundraising drives. Digital content creation (e.g. graphics, podcast clips). Maintaining and updating our CRM records including donor information. Managing our inboxes to connect to supporters and steward our members. Full advert here: https://www.compassonline.org.uk/digital-engagement-officer/ Closing Date : 3 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates The application deadline is 5pm and we expect interviews to be held in September. item.title: Membership and Communications Coordinator
item.description: The Association for Citizenship Teaching (ACT) is the national subject association for Citizenship education. We support teachers, schools and education leaders through professional development, curriculum resources, research and policy engagement, helping ensure every young person receives a high-quality Citizenship education. This is an exciting time to join ACT. Following the Government's Curriculum and Assessment Review, Citizenship education is being strengthened across secondary education and introduced as a statutory subject in primary schools for the first time. ACT is working closely with government, parliamentarians and education partners to help shape the future of the subject. We are looking for a Membership and Communications Coordinator to join our small, friendly and collaborative team. The role combines membership administration, customer service and digital communications. You will be the first point of contact for many of our members while supporting the delivery of communications across email, website and social media. Key responsibilities include: Providing excellent membership administration and customer service. Maintaining and developing our CRM database and membership records. Supporting email marketing and member communications. Drafting and publishing website and social media content. Supporting marketing campaigns and membership growth. Providing administrative support across communications, events and organisational projects. Monitoring membership and engagement data to inform decision making. We're looking for someone with excellent organisational and communication skills, experience of administration or customer service, strong attention to detail and an interest in communications, marketing and education. As a small national charity, every member of our team makes a meaningful contribution. This is an excellent opportunity to develop a broad range of skills while working alongside teachers, policymakers and education organisations to strengthen Citizenship education across England. item.title: Campaigns Lead
item.description: This is a new role at ECU, being recruited as part of a wider programme of work to deepen the relationships between national organisations working on economic systems change and grassroots campaigners. The Campaigns Lead will work closely with the Head of Campaigns on driving forward our high-impact campaigns for economic systems change. For at least the first year, the Campaigns Lead will be working primarily on our coalition campaign on the cost of living crisis, Cost of Living Action. The campaign, which is currently made up of over 40 organisations from across civil society, unions and grassroots groups, aims to end the cost of living crisis and put in place solutions to prevent it from ever happening again. It focuses on our policy demands in five areas that drive the cost of living crisis: wages, social security, energy, housing and taxation. The campaign positions itself as the civil society coalition focused on the cost of living as a whole, and that solutions to it must be addressed that way. The campaign relaunched in early 2026 and has a vital role to play in putting media and political pressure on the government to take action. We also work closely with those most impacted by the crisis and aim to centre the voices of those with lived experience of economic hardship in all that we do. This role will shape and drive forward a programme of impactful communications, advocacy and other campaigning activities under the rebooted campaign to secure transformative changes that bring real improvement to people’s lives. There is ample opportunity to engage politically in this role, increasing as you develop in the position. The full description and job pack can be found here: https://www.econchange.org/recruitment/campaigns-lead Closing Date : 17 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates The closing time for applications is 9am Application Details Apply via Workable here: https://apply.workable.com/j/CC55514278 Website : http://www.econchange.org/

item.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
item.description: The Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (PIIRS) at Princeton University is pleased to announce the call for applications to the PIIRS Postdoctoral Fellowship Program for the 2027-28 academic year. As a leading global institution in interdisciplinary research on international issues, PIIRS is dedicated to advancing innovative scholarship that addresses the world's most pressing challenges. The PIIRS Postdoctoral Fellows Program is integral to that mission. We will award up to four postdoctoral fellowships to our 2027-28 cohort. PIIRS seeks recent PhDs in the Social Sciences who have demonstrated exceptional scholarship, congruent with the Institute's intellectual focus, that simultaneously advances theoretical debates in their disciplinary field; creatively speaks to and engages with a multidisciplinary audience; and deepens substantive regional knowledge of specific places. Appointments will be made at the rank of Postdoctoral Research Associate and are for one year (12 months) with the possibility of renewal pending satisfactory performance and continued funding. Postdoctoral Research Associates are expected to be in residence at Princeton or the local vicinity for the entire academic year or demonstrate to the program’s satisfaction the ability to be on campus on a daily basis and on short notice in order to fulfill responsibilities relating to in-person participation. The position requires Postdoctoral Research Associates to be on campus at least four days per week. Leveraging Princeton's scholarly resources, fellows will focus on research, expand their intellectual horizons, and prepare work for publication. They will have biweekly meetings with the faculty director to share their work, and monthly meetings with faculty fellows from various social sciences to present their work and learn from others. Fellows are also encouraged to engage with colleagues and attend departmental seminars. Applicants must demonstrate outstanding scholarly achievement and promise. To be eligible, applicants generally cannot have more than two years of postdoctoral experience prior to the start of the appointment, at the beginning of the academic year on September 1, 2027. The postdoctoral selection will be made based on the strength of the candidates' scholarly record; the promise of the proposed research; and the ability to contribute to the intellectual life of the postdoctoral program (with interest in connecting with other PIIRS and Princeton departments on campus). In addition to a competitive salary and benefits, the program will provide the Fellow with the opportunity to host a small, pre-publication, book workshop; and a research fund of $4,000 per year. The program will also provide shared office space, and a laptop computer. Further information can be found at here . This position is subject to the University's background check policy. The work location for this position is in-person on campus at Princeton University. Position is not eligible for sponsorship of an H-1B visa requiring consular processing; other visa sponsorships (including H-1B visas not requiring consular processing) may be available, as appropriate. Application Instructions Applications are due by September 15, 2026 (11:59 p.m. EST). The following application items should be uploaded by the applicant: Cover letter Curriculum vitae Transcripts Research Proposal indicating plans for two-year postdoc (maximum 5 pages double-spaced) Dissertation abstract (including Table of Contents) Writing sample: one chapter of the dissertation or one published article related to dissertation topic. Document confirming either that you have completed all requirements for the PhD degree or a letter signed by your dissertation advisor indicating that you will complete the PhD by the start date of the fellowship. The names and email addresses of three referees, who will be contacted automatically by the online application system with an invitation to upload their letter of recommendation to the system by the application deadline. (**Please note: all letters of reference should be submitted by your referees before September 15, 2026. deadline. **) Equal Employment Opportunity Statement Princeton University is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

item.title: Public Affairs and Campaigns Officer (North)
item.description: The Royal British Legion is looking for a confident and politically aware Public Affairs and Campaigns Officer to lead impactful campaigning activity across the North of England, including North East, North West, and Yorkshire & the Humber regions of England. This is an opportunity to work at the heart of issues affecting the Armed Forces community, turning insight into action and ensuring the voices of veterans, serving personnel and their families are heard where it matters most. From influencing local decision-makers to shaping meaningful conversations across communities, you’ll play a visible role in driving positive change on behalf of those who have served. We’re looking for someone who understands how local government and public affairs really work; someone who can build credibility quickly, spot opportunities to influence and create campaigns that connect with people on a local level. You’ll be equally comfortable briefing MPs and councillors, working alongside community stakeholders, organising events and translating national priorities into campaigns that feel relevant and tangible within local communities. This role would suit someone who thrives on relationship-building, enjoys working across a varied political landscape and has the confidence to represent a nationally respected organisation in high-profile settings. In return, you’ll join a passionate and collaborative team working on issues that genuinely matter. No two days will look the same, and the impact of your work will be visible across the region. Whether you’re developing local campaign networks, supporting Armed Forces Covenant activity or helping influence policy conversations at a grassroots level, you’ll have the freedom to bring fresh thinking, new ideas and your own approach to engagement. If you’re motivated by purpose, skilled at influencing others and want to be part of an organisation committed to making a lasting difference to the Armed Forces community, we’d love to hear from you. item.title: Caseworker (20hrs)
item.description: Adam Dance MP, Member of Parliament for Yeovil, was elected as the Liberal Democrat MP for Yeovil in July 2024, and is looking for an enthusiastic, professional and organised person to join his team as a caseworker (20 hours). The role will be based in his Yeovil office, and is an exciting opportunity to join a friendly, supportive team and become an integral part of supporting consituents. Responsibilities will include: Dealing with a large number of standard queries by telephone, email or face-to-face Managing and progressing a varied portfolio of casework, including logging cases, taking appropriate actions promptly and monitoring progress Drafting enquiries to government agencies on behalf of constituents Policy research on complex issues Maintaining up-to-date knowledge of relevant guidelines and legislation as appropriate in dealing with casework Competent use of IT including casework management system & Microsoft Office Accompanying the MP to advice surgeries and visits in the constituency Essential criteria: A good knowledge of Yeovil & South Somerset and the services available to local people Strong written, communication and analytical skills with a good telephone manner and attention to detail Excellent command of written English is required to produce high quality correspondence, representing the MP in letters and emails Experience of keeping professional notes and accurate records Ability to carry out tasks quickly and to a high standard Highly desirable criteria: Previous experience of working in a similar role Flexibility to work on the occasional evening and weekend will be required, which will be compensated with time off in lieu. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 4 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews/Assessments to be held wc 21st September 2026 Application Details Accepted applications must include the below: • Covering letter (max 1 side of A4) explaining why you would like to work for Adam Dance MP and what you can bring to the constituency team • An up to date CV (max 2 sides of A4) • Contact details of two referees and confirmation of any notice period you would need to give if in employment Please apply by email with the subject line "Caseworker Application YOUR NAME" to Kate.alford@parliament.uk Website : https://www.yeovil-libdems.org.uk/adam-dance

item.title: Constituency Support Officer
item.description: Dr Allison Gardner MP is seeking an enthusiastic & highly organised Constituency Support Officer. This is a varied, hands-on role suited to someone who enjoys no two days being the same. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: • Provide high-quality support to constituents by responding to enquiries and progressing casework. • Draft correspondence on behalf of the MP • Support the smooth day-to-day running of the constituency office, including administration and data entry • Assist with organising constituency visits, meetings, street surgeries, advice surgeries, leafleting sessions and community events. • Attend meetings and events across the constituency with the MP • Undertake research/prepare briefings to support the MP's constituency work. • Build & maintain positive working relationships with local organisations, public bodies and community groups. • Provide flexible support across the office & helping wherever required. • Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. ABOUT YOU: The successful candidate will be: • An organised, dependable all-rounder. • An excellent communicator with strong written English and exceptional attention to detail. • Able to manage competing priorities/remain calm under pressure. • Friendly and confident when dealing with members of the public. • Able to exercise sound judgement, maintain discretion and handle confidential information. • A self-starter who can work independently while contributing positively to a small, busy team. • Passionate about delivering excellent service to constituents and supporting local communities. • Flexible and willing to work outside normal office hours when required, including regular Saturday working to support constituency events, advice surgeries/community engagement ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS • A full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle. • Excellent organisational, interpersonal and administrative skills. • Strong IT skills • The right to work in the UK. • Sympathy with the aims and values of the Labour Party. DESIRABLE • Strong knowledge of Stoke-on-Trent South & the surrounding area. • Previous experience in a customer-facing, public service or administrative role. • Experience of working in a fast-paced environment Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 31 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Applications close at 5.00pm Interviews may take place before the closing date, and early applications are encouraged. Application Details Please send: • Your CV; and • A covering letter (maximum one page) explaining why you are interested in the role and how your experience meets the requirements of the position. Applications should be sent to allison.gardner.mp@parliament.uk with the subject line: APPLICATION – CONSTITUENCY SUPPORT OFFICER If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know and we will be happy to discuss your needs. Website : http://allisongardner.co.uk

item.title: Communications & Campaigns Manager (Stakeholder Communications)
item.description: About the role You’ll manage reputation-focused communications and campaigns for a range of external audiences and internal stakeholders. You’ll lead stakeholder communications activity, support partnership PR initiatives, and create clear, persuasive content across online and offline channels. You’ll report to the Head of Communications & Campaigns and work closely with colleagues across the organisation to translate complex marine conservation work into accessible, engaging multi-channel narratives. What you’ll do - Build the organisation’s reputation and reach through strong internal and external communications. - Lead stakeholder communications for campaigns, projects and partnership PR initiatives. - Develop narratives, write and edit copy, and shape content for a wide range of audiences and channels. - Manage internal communications activity. - Act as communications lead for events such as the AGM. - Maintain an integrated communications calendar and support KPI reporting for communications outputs. - Provide storytelling, reputation positioning and science communication support across the organisation. About you You’ll be an experienced communications professional who can build relationships, manage competing priorities and create content that is accurate, accessible and inspiring. - Experience managing internal and external communications across different channels and audiences. - Knowledge of stakeholder communications, relationship management and campaign delivery. - A proven track record of writing and editing reader-friendly articles, publications and reports. - Experience developing storytelling and reputation-positioning narratives, including translating scientific or technical content for general audiences. - Excellent organisation, attention to detail and time management. - Confidence working under scrutiny, particularly where reputation or media interest is involved. How you’ll work This is a remote, full-time role with occasional travel to external meetings and events, so you’ll need to live in the UK and have appropriate eligibility to work. You’ll need to be comfortable working from home with remote teams, using your initiative and knowing when to involve senior colleagues. Closing Date : 30 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Application Details https://app.webrecruit.co/JobSeeker/ApplyOnline?jobid=147193&boardid=1778 Website : https://www.mcsuk.org/

item.title: Parliamentary Researcher/Senior Parliamentary Researcher
item.description: Jonathan Hinder MP is looking for an outstanding parliamentary researcher/senior parliamentary researcher, to be part of his team serving the people of Pendle and Clitheroe. This position will be primarily focused on Jonathan’s parliamentary and national political activity, but will involve close working with staff based in the constituency office to run local campaigns. Given the nature of the work there is a need for flexibility in working hours/occasional travel to the constituency. This will be based in the MP’s office in Westminster, working alongside a communications officer. Broad alignment with Jonathan’s political principles is essential. Key Responsibilities: Drive forward Jonathan's national political campaigns, working closely with other MPs’ offices, campaign groups and policy organisations. Manage Jonathan’s Westminster diary, ensuring time is allocated according to his priorities. Closely monitor parliamentary business and political developments in Westminster, ensuring Jonathan is informed of relevant breaking news. Undertake research, draft briefings and provide political advice. Draft speeches and prepare Jonathan for media appearances, working in tandem with the communications officer. Develop and maintain relationships with individuals and groups on Jonathan’s behalf. Attend parliamentary meetings and engagements either with or on Jonathan’s behalf. Deal with complex policy queries in conjunction with the constituency team. Work collaboratively with the constituency team to deliver on local priorities. Skills Required: An excellent understanding of British politics, including an in-depth knowledge of the Labour Party’s history, different traditions, and internal dynamics. Highly motivated, eager to learn quickly and take on new challenges. Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, capable of engaging diverse audiences and speaking with the authority of the MP. Strong political judgement, with a clear understanding of people’s priorities in an area like Pendle & Clitheroe. Ability to work swiftly and independently without supervision, with a strong eye for detail and accuracy. Team player, happy working as part of a close-knit team. A knowledge of the Pendle and Clitheroe constituency and its political dynamics is desirable but not essential. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 28 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis from the opening of applications. Start date is as soon as possible. Application Details E-mail katie.fisher@parliament.uk a CV & one page cover letter (“Your name - Parliamentary Researcher Application” in the subject line) Website : https://www.jonathanhinder.com/

item.title: Assistant Professor of International Relations (Tenure-Track)
item.description: The Department of Political Science at Northwestern University seeks applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor in International Relations to begin on September 1, 2027. We seek candidates who will advance international relations scholarship and engage with important issues in contemporary world politics. The successful applicant will teach a combination of graduate and undergraduate courses. A Ph.D. in Political Science or a closely related field, with International Relations training, is required. ABD applicants who anticipate completion of the doctorate by Fall 2027 will be considered. Applicants must provide a curriculum vitae, cover letter, writing sample, research statement, teaching statement, and three letters of recommendation. Review of applications will begin immediately, and all applications received by September 15 will be given full consideration. To apply, click the 'Apply' button For inquiries about job advertisements or the application process, please contact Stephen Monteiro, Business Administrator in the Political Science Department. stephen.monteiro@northwestern.edu . Salary The expected base pay range for this position is $100,000 - $125,000. This base pay range is for a nine-month academic appointment, does not include summer salary, and is subject to negotiation. Northwestern University has provided a pay range representing its good faith estimate of what the university reasonably expects to pay for the position. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate including years since terminal degree, training, and field or discipline; departmental budget availability; internal equity; and external market pay for comparable jobs. Benefits At Northwestern, we are proud to provide meaningful and competitive benefits. The available benefits package for this position will include health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance; paid medical/sick and parental leave; tuition benefits for the employee and dependents; pre-tax and flex spending accounts for commuting and dependent care; generous retirement savings options; and wellness programs. For a comprehensive overview of available benefits, including eligibility details, visit us at Northwestern Benefits to learn more. Northwestern University is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics, including disability and veteran status. View Northwestern’s non-discrimination statement . Job applicants who wish to request an accommodation in the application or hiring process should contact the Office of Civil Rights and Title IX Compliance. View additional information on the accommodations process .

item.title: Research Assistant/Associate - Postdoctoral Researcher in Modern Dravidian Studies (Fixed Term)
item.description: The Faculty of History wishes to recruit a Research Assistant/Research Associate within the broad field of 'Modern Dravidian History and Politics 1945-to the present, working under the supervision of Professor Shruti Kapila, Professor of History and Politics. The position is endowed by a recent bequest to the School of Humanities and Social Sciences. This is a full-time post for three years, commencing 1 October 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter. The pathways and aims of this research are to build historical and analytical perspectives on welfare in relation to shifts in democracy and statecraft including emerging digital public infrastructure. A combination of methods - archival, data sets and interview based will be essential. The interaction of ideas and institutions with public perception, political languages and democratic outcome will be key. The ideal candidate will be educated to PhD level, with established expertise in South Asian/Tamil history or politics (or clear evidence that completion of such a doctorate is imminent) and will have fluency with the use of research materials in English and Tamil; proven ability to conduct and deliver a high quality research project; be an experienced Microsoft office user, prepared to learn other software tools if required and have the ability and willingness to engage in digital humanities research and public -facing work, in a collaborative and inter-disciplinary capacity. The postholder will undertake innovative research with data sets, archives and interviews on welfare, democracy and postcolonial statecraft and other repositories utilising Tamil language. With the supervision of Professor Shruti Kapila, they will: Write research articles where appropriate from their own work and move towards publishing a monograph at the completion of their postdoctoral fellowship. Work with Prof Kapila on to identify key sources for digital humanities research and to design and manage the public platform for the project as required. Work closely and collaboratively with colleagues including doctoral students and postdoctoral fellows; and further afield, academics, public intellectuals and others. Fully participate in workshops and conferences connected to the project by presenting papers and assisting with arrangements; attend other conferences, held by other associations and groups, when possible. Work with and inter-disciplinary research and writing with a view to presenting ideas and policy perspectives to stakeholders, public and scholarly audiences. Engage with tasks connected to the dissemination activities of the project. More information about the Faculty is available here: https://www.hist.cam.ac.uk/ Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available until 30 September 2029 in the first instance. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click the 'Apply' button above. Informal enquiries are welcomed and should be directed to: Professor Shruti Kapila ( sk555@cam.ac.uk ) If you have any queries regarding the application process, please contact: hr@hist.cam.ac.uk Please quote reference JJ50616 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.
item.dc:creator: University of Cambridge

item.title: Digital Communications Officer
item.description: Family Rights Group’s mission is to create a more socially just society in which the child welfare and family justice systems support children to live safely and thrive within their family, while strengthening the family and community networks of those children who cannot live at home. Founded in 1974, our work combines commitment to human rights and social justice with expertise in child welfare law, policy and practice. As Family Rights Group’s Digital Communications Officer, you will work to plan, develop and deliver a range of informed, creative, impactful and accessible digital content for our external audiences to increase visibility and engagement with the charity’s work and to meet our strategic objectives. You will be responsible for the ideation, production, editing, and publishing of standout content that reaches diverse audiences, including policy-makers and politicians, donors and supporters, and families with experience of the child welfare system, as well as the wider public. You will oversee the day-to-day management of our social media channels (Instagram, Facebook, BlueSky and LinkedIn), developing our digital presence, engaging with our target audiences, and increasing the charity’s reach. Communications at Family Rights Group is a team effort. You will work closely with colleagues across Family Rights Group, and particularly with our Content Creator and Digital Marketing Strategist in our Public Affairs and Communications team. You will collaborate on a dynamic, diverse content plan that amplifies our mission, with a focus on the voices and experiences of families and young people. This is a hands-on role that requires a strong interest in the child welfare system and our mission, combined with the technical expertise to be able to develop written and audio-visual content. Closing Date : 4 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates The closing time for applications is 9am. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an online interview the following week. The starting date is as soon as possible after appointment, depending on the appointee's notice period. Application Details To apply, please go to the following page on our website: https://frg.org.uk/about-us/work-for-us/digital-communications-officer/ You will find more details including the full JD of the role, and application form to complete. Website : http://frg.org.uk

item.title: Parliamentary Caseworkers - Interim and Short-Term Assignments
item.description: Hive Support is a Community Interest Company providing specialist HR, recruitment and operational support to Members of Parliament and their offices. As a not-for-profit, we exist to strengthen the way parliamentary offices are staffed and run, and we work with MPs across Westminster and the constituencies to do that. We regularly provide experienced, short-term staffing support to MPs' offices, and demand for interim cover is growing. We are expanding our pool of experienced parliamentary professionals available for short-term assignments. We are particularly keen at present to hear from experienced caseworkers , though we welcome registrations across all parliamentary roles These opportunities typically arise to cover: Sickness absence Annual leave Short-term increases in workload Interim support during recruitment processes Assignments can vary in length, from a few weeks to several months, and may be offered on a full-time, part-time or flexible basis. Most roles can be undertaken remotely, while others may require a Westminster or constituency presence. Who we're looking for We are keen to hear from individuals who: Have prior experience working in a parliamentary office Can step into a role quickly and operate effectively with limited onboarding Are confident managing competing priorities in a fast-paced environment Have strong drafting and communication skills Experience may include: Casework IPSA and payroll processes Communications and press Research and policy Office management or Chief of Staff responsibilities Constituency support Secondments and additional work If you are currently employed by an MP, please note that your MP will need to approve any additional work under your IPSA contract. We encourage you to be clear on any contractual or procedural requirements in advance. We recognise that many candidates bring valuable transferable skills that are highly relevant to parliamentary roles, and we would be pleased to consider such applications for other opportunities we advertise. However, due to the nature of these short-term assignments, this registration is only open to individuals who have worked for a Member of Parliament within the last three years. Closing Date : 6 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Register your interest to join our talent pool. We will contact you when suitable short-term roles arise. These are often filled quickly, so please respond promptly when we get in touch, as we may need to move on to other candidates if we do not hear back soon. Application Details To apply, please submit your CV, clearly outlining your parliamentary experience: https://recruitment.hivesupport.co.uk/apply/35054/experienced-parliamentary-staff-register-for-short-term-opportunities Website : https://hivesupport.co.uk/

item.title: Training Coordinator
item.description: The Knowledge Exchange Group requires a Training Coordinator to join our dynamic team. The successful candidate will be an organised and efficient team player. You will be reliable, comfortable with technology and have good commercial skills. You’ll have some experience of events or training, however we will provide full training and development to ensure you succeed in this role. You will organise and oversee the smooth delivery of training courses, ranging in size from 5-50 attendees. You will collaborate closely with the Director, marketing, product and operations teams to ensure commercial success. To include: • Developing and managing relationships with trainers and clients. • Agreeing and negotiating trainer fees, within fixed budgets. • Liaising with trainers to create course copy and materials. Chasing biographies, course materials, and presentations. • To build course websites and email templates. • Sending and coordinating pre-event questionnaires. • Ensuring courses are CPD certified. • Sending joining instructions to delegates, delivering customer and technical support, by phone, email or online. • Post-course follow up – to distribute evaluation forms and analyse results. To record costs and process trainer invoices. • To set up webinars on Zoom and arrange tech checks. • Client liaison for inhouse training. Personal Attributes and Experience: • Six months work experience in a professional setting. • Evidence of previous events/training experience. • Educated to degree level, minimum 2:1 or similar • Excellent IT skills e.g. Microsoft Office, Zoom. • Previous use of a virtual event platform (desirable), basic graphic design skills (desirable), email marketing or website building (desirable). • Excellent planning and organisational skills, accurate and meticulous. • Excellent customer service skills, enthusiastic and helpful approach. • Negotiation and commercial skills. • Reliable, good problem-solving skills. • A team player. • A good communicator, able to build relationships. Benefits: • 23 days’ annual holiday entitlement rising to 25 after 2 years continuous service and 28 days after 3 years (carry over up to 3 days) • Company pension scheme • Flexible working • Dynamic and agile team • Hybrid working Closing Date : 28 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will be conducted from the 24th August. item.title: Political Advisor
item.description: Hours: 37 Hours Per Week About the Role Are you interested in working in a political environment within a Local Unitary Authority? If so, then this could be the job for you! We are looking for an engaging, experienced and committed individual to join us as a Political Advisor for the Reform Group. This is an exciting and unique opportunity to provide a variety of services to the Reform Group, ranging from policy research and development to supporting senior Reform councillors in their strategic aims. You will be involved in note taking, organising meetings as well as assisting with wider duties required of you. You will provide high-quality political advice, policy research, and strategic support to the Reform Group Leader and Members of the Group, enabling effective decision‑making, policy development, and representation within the Council and across wider political and stakeholder networks. Sitting within the Governance Teams at the Council, you will act as a key link between the political group, council officers, and external partners, ensuring clear communication, alignment of priorities, and effective collaboration, including engagement with national and sector‑wide political structures. What We Are Looking For We are looking for someone who has: Experience and knowledge of providing high quality support to a team and working with others to complete projects to a high standard and on time. You will be highly organised with great ICT, English language and time management skills. You’ll be an effective communicator across the organisation, from residents and officers to senior managers and politicians. Experience of working in a political environment is desirable, as is a sound understanding of local government and its governance. Full support in all aspects of the role will be provided. Your work time will largely be based at the Civic Offices in Grays, Essex, with some opportunity to work from home. You may be expected to attend some evening events across the year. item.title: Campaigns Officer
item.description: Location: Hybrid – minimum 2 days per week from London office and 2 days per month from the BVRLA office, River Lodge, Amersham, Bucks, HP7 0DD. Some UK travel and occasional overnight stays required. About the role The BVRLA is looking for a Campaigns Officer to support its award-nominated public affairs and campaign work. Working with our Public Affairs Manager in the Policy and Research team, you will support policy engagement campaigns, member mobilisation, political relationships and raising the profile of our work. You will join a talented, highly motivated and supportive team and work across fast-moving policy areas including electric vehicles, decarbonisation, future mobility, consumer finance and motor taxation. Key Tasks and Responsibilities Engage with MPs and staff, Select Committees and industry stakeholders to raise awareness of BVRLA, its members and policy priorities. Coordinate campaigns, strategies and programmes supporting BVRLA’s policy aims. Represent BVRLA at external working groups, conferences and third-party events. Support members to engage with MPs through the ‘Industry Champions’ programme. Lead BVRLA’s technical understanding of Bills passing through the Commons and Lords. Provide high-quality policy briefings for colleagues, MPs and members. Work with communications, compliance, training and events teams to maximise impact with Government, media and stakeholders. Distil BVRLA political and operational insight into accessible content for members. Provide content and administrative support for research projects, meetings and events. Professional and personal requirements Strong written and verbal communication skills. Solid understanding of UK Parliament, politics, procedure and policymaking. Self-starter with initiative, drive and creativity, able to multitask and engage potential new members. At least 1 year’s experience in a political environment, ideally in consultancy, think tank, media, trade association or Parliament. Excellent research skills, with the ability to distil complex topics into clear, accessible content for different audiences. Grit, determination and willingness to stretch themselves, learn and develop. Confident in media and social media relations, with the ability to support media coverage and reputation management. item.title: Senior Policy Officer
item.description: The NHS Alliance’s policy and analysis team shapes national policy and influences decision makers using evidence, expertise, and a deep understanding of our members’ experiences and aspirations for the NHS. We connect members and policymakers, provide clear and credible insight, and offer practical, workable solutions that respond to frontline realities. Through this, we strengthen our members’ collective voice and help ensure they can deliver the best possible care. We are looking for a senior policy officer to support the delivery of policy projects and contribute to the achievement of The NHS Alliance’s policy objectives. You will help to analyse policy developments and deliver projects to influence and translate government policy on behalf of members. As a senior policy officer, you will: Support the delivery of member-informed influencing activity and respond quickly to emerging issues. Observe, analyse and describe policy developments and their implications for members and the NHS. Work collaboratively with colleagues in other directorates and reflect wider NHS Alliance policy positions in content and activity. Draft policy content, such as reports, notes and briefings, and present work at internal meetings. Support delivery and scoping of funded projects, working with the commercial team when needed and provide administrative support where required. Support stakeholder and member engagement by preparing briefings, taking notes and sharing intelligence internally. Develop relationships with members and be comfortable working with senior NHS leaders. item.title: Research Manager
item.description: Join Us and Help Shape Brighter Futures At Depaul UK, we believe in people’s potential — and we take action every day to help unlock it. Whether you’re supporting young people directly or strengthening our organisation behind the scenes, your work will create real, lasting impact. Research Manager Ready to use research to drive real social change? Join us and lead high-impact research that influences policy, strengthens services, and amplifies the voices of people experiencing homelessness. You'll design and deliver robust mixed-methods research, turning data and lived experience into compelling evidence that shapes decisions and creates lasting impact. You will be an experienced researcher with strong qualitative and quantitative research skills, excellent analytical and writing ability, and a track record of delivering high-quality projects from concept to publication. You'll be confident managing multiple priorities, building relationships with stakeholders, and transforming complex findings into clear, meaningful insights. By joining our values-led organisation that is committed to ending homelessness, you'll have the opportunity to influence change at a national level, work flexibly as part of a collaborative team, and contribute to research that makes a tangible difference to people's lives. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. Please note that this job opportunity is offered as a full-time (37.5 hours per week), permanent basis. In addition, this job offers a Hybrid working arrangement (in the office two days per week) working from one of our regions (London, Manchester or the North East); therefore, we welcome applications from different parts of the country. You will need to be able to travel throughout the UK and on occasions work out of hours. item.title: Parliamentary Assistant
item.description: The Rt Hon Graham Stuart MP is looking to recruit an organised, politically aware and highly motivated Parliamentary Assistant to join his team. This is an excellent opportunity to support the parliamentary work of an active constituency MP. The successful candidate will undertake research, prepare detailed briefings and help ensure Graham is fully informed on parliamentary, policy and constituency matters. The successful candidate will have excellent research and written communication skills, strong organisational skills, with experience of diary management and the ability to manage a varied workload in a fast-paced environment. Key Responsibilities Manage Graham's diary and ensure all entries are accurate and complete. Analyse, evaluate and interpret data to ensure Graham is accurately informed on key issues Assist in writing external communications including speeches. Compilation of briefing packs, take notes of meetings and draft appropriate submissions Develop and maintain current knowledge on relevant areas of parliamentary business and the local constituency. Engage confidentially, professionally, with care and integrity with members of the public, through telephone enquiries, social media, email and face to face Have working knowledge of relevant legislation and upcoming business including how they impact on the constituency Maintain positive on-going relationships with all parties including members of the public, groups, suppliers and Westminster where required Prepare and present briefing notes for committees, press releases, parliamentary questions etc. Respond to routine correspondence, including campaign emails and casework. item.title: Caseworker/Senior Caseworker
item.description: Deirdre Costigan MP is seeking a Caseworker/Senior Caseworker to join her team, based in the Constituency Office in Southall with occasional work in Parliament. The successful candidate will support the team in managing constituency casework and contributing to wider policy and campaign work. The role includes liaising with government departments, local authorities and other organisations, drafting mass policy correspondence and identifying trends in casework to help inform parliamentary priorities. Key responsibilities Assist with arranging and attending MP advice surgeries, coffee mornings, community events and follow up as appropriate. Handle a high volume of routine enquiries and assist with more complex casework from members of the public via telephone, email and face-to-face interactions. Support Senior Caseworkers in progressing constituency casework and resolving constituent issues effectively. Research and draft mass campaign responses to constituents regarding government policy. Produce high-quality written responses to constituent enquiries. Identify trends and recurring issues arising from constituency casework and communicate these effectively to the Parliamentary team to help shape campaigns, policy priorities and parliamentary interventions. Ensure records are accurately maintained and information is managed confidentially in accordance with relevant data protection legislation. Ensure all cases are handled promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately, in accordance with the wishes and direction of the MP. Log all cases, monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are completed. Occasionally work outside normal office hours, including attending events with the MP when required. Essential Criteria Excellent written communication skills and the ability to draft letters and emails to a high professional standard. A proactive approach to work, both independently and as part of a small team. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and manage competing priorities. Commitment to the aims and values of the Labour Party. Desirable Criteria Previous casework experience. Experience of using casework management software. Ealing Southall is a very diverse constituency and knowledge of a relevant community language, e.g. Punjabi would be desirable. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 26 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Expected interview period - First two weeks of September (subject to confirmation) Application Details Please submit a two page CV and one page cover letter to deirdre.costigan.mp@parliament.uk with the subject line Caseworker application 2026 by 12pm on closing date . The cover letter should highlight how your values, experience and skills meet the job specification. We value diversity and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds. We are unable to accept late applications or provide feedback at application stage. Website : http://members.parliament.uk/member/5075/contact

item.title: Senior Caseworker
item.description: Chris Murray is looking to recruit an experienced caseworker to join his team in Edinburgh and manage the office’s casework output and processes. The Senior Caseworker will support Chris to be an active, impactful and approachable MP. You will lead the casework function and work with a Caseworker to provide advice and support to local people on a range of issues. Managing a large caseload, organising MP surgeries, and supporting relevant events, you will help resolve problems for local people through communication with government agencies, local authorities, the voluntary sector and other organisations. The successful candidate will be a proven problem solver with a high level of written and verbal communication. Existing experience within a casework environment would be an advantage and what is essential is the ability to deal with high volumes of correspondence combined with a genuine concern for the lives of the constituents. The key responsibilities are as follows: • Assist with surgeries and other meetings and follow up as appropriate • Ensure all cases are logged; monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken • Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially and in line with data protection legislation • Exercise a level of autonomy in reaching decisions on cases based on the evidence • Gather relevant information to resolve or progress cases • Liaise with Government agencies, voluntary sector and others to resolve constituency matters • Manage a large caseload of complex cases, working in a professional, confidential, caring and sensitive manner • Respond professionally, sensitively, confidentially and with integrity to routine correspondence and enquiries by email, telephone, social media and face to face from constituents, the media, lobbyists and pressure groups Required skills and values: • Ability to deal with and prioritise a large and varied caseload, and work well under pressure • Ability to manage expectations in sometimes challenging circumstances • Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills • Ability to work independently as well as effectively as part of a small team • Ability and willingness to work outside of normal hours and travel for work occasionally • Sympathetic to the aims, values and objectives of the Labour Party Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). item.title: Caseworker
item.description: Miatta Fahnbulleh MP is looking for a dynamic and highly committed individual for the role of Caseworker in her busy Peckham Constituency office. Key Responsibilities will include: Assist with surgeries and other constituency meetings and follow up as appropriate. Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as assisting with more complex cases from members of the public by phone, email, social media or face to face. Ongoing communication may be required. Draft responses to constituents. Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately in accordance with the MP. Gather relevant information to assist with resolving cases. Log all cases; monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken. Retain records and information confidentially and in line with the Data Protection Act. Responsibility for managing the voicemails inbox. Essential Skills Required: Ability to prioritise and manage a large and varied caseload, working well under pressure. Handle complex, time-sensitive, and often emotive issues accurately, efficiently, and with empathy. Maintain comprehensive and accurate case records. Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills. Good IT skills, including experience with MS Office applications. Ability to write letters and emails to a high professional standard. Self-motivated with the ability to work independently, while also working effectively as part of a small team alongside the Senior Caseworker. Support the aims and values of The Labour Party. Additional information: There may be a requirement to work outside of normal hours, including evenings and weekends and occasional travel for work. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 28 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews expected to be held within two weeks of 7 September 2026, start date as soon as possible thereafter. Application Details Please include "Caseworker Application" in the subject line of your email. Applicants should submit a CV summary (no more than 2 pages) along with a cover letter (no more than 1 page) detailing how you meet the required skills for the position. Additionally, please provide the contact details of two references (one of whom must be your current or most recent employer). Send your application to sade.edinboro@parliament.uk Website : https://miattafahnbulleh.org/

item.title: Parliamentary Researcher
item.description: About the role I was elected in May 2026 to represent the Highlands and Islands, Scotland's largest parliamentary region. The people here face a distinct set of challenges: depopulation, a shortage of housing, centralised healthcare, inadequate infrastructure, and renewable energy projects reshaping rural and coastal communities — alongside the enduring concerns of fishing and farming. I'm looking for a bright, driven Parliamentary Researcher to join my team and help me stand up for them. It's a rare chance to get involved at an early stage across all of my work, in Parliament and across the Region, with real scope to grow and progress over the five-year term. What you'll do You'll start by supporting me across three areas, and take on more as you find your feet: Research: Dig into the policy, legislation and issues that matter to the Highlands and Islands, and get to grips with the facts and figures behind them Turn that into clear, accurate briefings and speaking notes for the chamber and beyond Communications: Draft press releases, articles and social media posts, and help run my Facebook and Instagram Help with local campaigns and day-to-day media enquiries Parliament: Draft parliamentary questions, motions and debate contributions Support the smooth running of my office and, as Reform's Parliamentary Business Manager, the group's business and Whips Office. About you Having done this job myself at Holyrood, I know that raw talent, drive and a genuine desire to learn count for far more than a polished CV. I'd happily take on someone with real ability and train them up. I expect parts of this role to be new to whomever I appoint, what matters is the ability to pick things up fast. You might be an ambitious graduate or early-career professional looking to work at the heart of Scottish politics. What I'm looking for: A sharp mind and the ability to learn quickly Strong writing, and a feel for turning detail into a clear argument Drive, initiative and sound judgement A real interest in politics, current affairs and the Highlands and Islands Desirable, but not essential: A strong connection to, or knowledge of, the local issues in the Highlands, Moray or the Islands Familiarity with video editing or graphics software (e.g. Adobe) — though a willingness to learn is enough Closing Date : 4 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will be held in person at the Scottish Parliament. These will be done on a rolling basis, so early applications are encouraged. Application Details Please send a CV and a short covering letter explaining your interest in the role to max.bannerman.msp@parliament.scot Website : https://reformuk.scot/
item.dc:creator: Max Bannerman MSP

item.title: Parliamentary Researcher
item.description: James Cartlidge, Conservative MP for South Suffolk and Shadow Secretary of State for Defence, is looking for a full-time Parliamentary Researcher to join his Westminster office. You will work in a small, busy team supporting the MP across his Shadow Cabinet responsibilities, with defence at the heart of the brief. This is a role for someone who can turn complex material into clear, usable writing at pace. You will be researching policy and legislation, drafting speeches, parliamentary questions and briefing packs, and keeping the MP ahead of developments in defence, foreign affairs and wider government policy. The pace is fast and the subject matter is high profile, so you will need to hold several deadlines at once without losing accuracy. A strong interest in or knowledge of defence, security and international affairs will serve you well. That said, we are just as interested in people who can research and write to a high standard from other policy backgrounds, so if that describes you, please apply. For full details please visit: https://recruitment.hivesupport.co.uk/job/35549/parliamentary-researcher-to-james-cartlidge-mp/london Closing Date : 31 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews: week commencing 7th September Start date: as soon as possible following pre-employment checks Application Details Apply online at: https://recruitment.hivesupport.co.uk/job/35549/parliamentary-researcher-to-james-cartlidge-mp/london Website : https://www.jamescartlidge.com/

item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: Sureena Brackenridge MP is looking for a highly motivated, politically aware and skilled communications professional to join her team as a Communications Officer. You will play an essential role in communicating Sureena’s work to constituents across Wolverhampton North East and supporting her as an active and visible MP. Based in the constituency office, you will work closely with the team to coordinate and deliver media, digital and campaign communications across Westminster and the constituency, demonstrating the impact of Sureena’s work. You will develop and deliver constituency campaigns, identifying opportunities to turn local issues and casework into campaigns, and producing communications that engage constituents and key stakeholders. You will monitor media and social media activity, identify opportunities, suggest creative content to grow reach and engagement, and analyse feedback and data to inform messaging and priorities. The role may be Part Time or Full Time, so please make clear your preference in the application. If you have experience in a communications or media environment, we would like to hear from you. The ideal candidate will have: • Excellent written and verbal communication skills • Strong experience in media, social media and/or digital communications • Strong digital content creation and delivery skills • Understanding of digital media trends and campaigning • Excellent research, analytical and problem-solving skills Key responsibilities: • Develop targeted communications and issue-based campaigns across a range of platforms • Monitor local, regional and national media and social media, identifying relevant issues, trends and opportunities • Create, edit and publish engaging digital and social media content • Identify opportunities to turn local issues and casework into campaigns • Draft external communications, press releases and public statements • Produce clear briefings, reports and follow-ups for meetings and events • Organise community surveys and analyse feedback to inform the Member’s work • Support stakeholder engagement and wider campaign activity • Maintain confidential records in line with the Data Protection Act • Undertake general office administration and work flexibly, including occasional evenings, weekends or travel Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . item.title: Parliamentary Assistant

The role will cover research, analysis, communications, parliamentary business, stakeholder engagement and general office support. Main responsibilities will include: • Researching parliamentary, national and local issues and assessing their impact on South Derbyshire. • Keeping up to date with parliamentary business, including legislation, Motions, debates and Hansard, and preparing briefings, speeches, parliamentary questions and other material for the MP. • Drafting articles, press releases and social media content, and monitoring media and social media for relevant issues and trends. • Attending meetings, taking notes and progressing actions. • Supporting diary management, correspondence, enquiries and general administration. • Building positive relationships with constituents, community groups, organisations and Westminster contacts. • Working with colleagues across communications and casework to ensure research and information are used effectively. • Maintaining accurate records and files in accordance with data protection requirements. Capabilities required: • Excellent communication, research, analytical and problem-solving skills. • Good political judgement and the ability to understand complex issues and their local impact. • Highly organised, adaptable and able to prioritise and work to tight deadlines. • A self-starter who can use initiative and work independently while contributing effectively to a small team. • Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage professionally and sensitively with the public. • Discretion, integrity and the ability to handle confidential information. • Strong IT and administrative skills. Desirable experience: Experience in a political, parliamentary, communications, public affairs or research environment; knowledge of Parliament and its processes; an understanding of South Derbyshire; and experience producing briefings, speeches, press releases or digital content. There may be a requirement to work outside normal hours and travel occasionally for work. item.title: Research Associate in the Politics of military labour association in Europe
item.description: We are looking to appoint a postdoctoral research associate with expertise in military power, military work and labour, the politics of unions, and/or critical and feminist approaches, to contribute to the delivery of a research project on the politics of military labour association and military unionisation in Europe. This is an excellent opportunity for a postdoctoral researcher to undertake research at the intersection of critical military studies, critical and feminist international relations and political economy, and to contribute to the development of scholarship on and knowledge exchange and impact relating to the politics of military labour. The role will involve reviewing and synthesising academic literature, data collection (conducting interviews and creating a corpus of texts from contemporary and archival sources), qualitative data analysis, knowledge exchange and impact activities, contributing to the organisation of events, and writing outputs for academic and non-academic audiences. We are seeking a candidate with a PhD (at or near completion) in politics, international relations, political economy or a cognate field and with expertise in relation to military power, military work and labour, the politics of unions, and/or critical and feminist approaches. Candidates should have experience producing high quality research and writing, the ability to write for different audiences, experience with qualitative social science methodologies, effective communication skills, the ability to contribute to event organisation, and the ability to work independently and closely with a team. Experience working with non-academic partners and stakeholders would be desirable. The project, funded by a standard grant from the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC), will be based in the School of Sociological Studies, Politics and International Relations and led by Dr Joanna Tidy. The successful candidate will join a our large and collegial School and will become part of our internationally recognised research community. You will join one or more of our active and supportive research clusters (for instance, political economy or international politics) and there are opportunities for interdisciplinary engagement across the Faculty and University.
item.dc:creator: University of Sheffield

item.title: Hatton Professorship of Sustainability
item.description: The Board of Electors to the Hatton Professorship of Sustainability invite applications for this Professorship from persons whose work falls within the general field of the Professorship (combining behavioural sciences and sustainability studies) to take up appointment on 1 July 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. Candidates will have an outstanding research record of international stature in a relevant area of study (includes experimental psychology, social neuroscience, behavioural economics, consumer behaviour, political science, policy studies, and environmental social sciences, as well as allied disciplines). The ideal candidate will demonstrate a commitment to the applications of research to address real world sustainability problems, working in combination with governments, businesses and civil society partners to design and monitor the impacts of interventions. They will be solution orientated with a special focus on individual, corporate and collective action towards environmental sustainability. They will be expected to demonstrate the vision, leadership, experience and enthusiasm to build on current strengths in maintaining and developing a leading research presence. They will hold a PhD or equivalent postgraduate qualification. Standard professorial duties include teaching and research, examining, supervision and administration. The Professor will be based in Cambridge. A competitive salary will be offered. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click 'Apply' above. Further information is available at: http://www.hr.admin.cam.ac.uk or contact the Human Resources, University Offices, The Old Schools, Cambridge, CB2 1TT, (email: professorships@admin.cam.ac.uk ). Applications, consisting of a letter of application, a statement of current and future research plans, a curriculum vitae and a publications list, along with details of three referees should be made online no later than 5 October 2026. Informal enquiries may be directed to Professor Bhaskar Vira (Convenor of Board of Electors): ProVCEducation@admin.cam.ac.uk Please quote reference LA50727 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

item.title: Assistant Professor in Comparative Politics
item.description: The School of Government and International Affairs (SGIA) at Durham University seeks to appoint an exceptional scholar as an Assistant Professor with research and teaching expertise in Comparative Politics, whose work uses quantitative research methods and has a regional focus on Africa, Asia, Latin America or the Middle East. This post offers an exciting opportunity to make a major contribution to the development of internationally excellent research and teaching while allowing unrivalled opportunities to progress and embed your career in an exciting and progressive institution. For more information, please visit our School page at School of Government and International Affairs - Durham University as well as the web page of the Centre for Institutions and Political Behaviour - Durham University The successful candidate will benefit from individual research support funding, access to SGIA and University-wide research funding and be entitled to apply for sabbatical leave on a basis of one term of leave in each seven terms of service. SGIA and Durham University provides high-quality administrative support to assist with applications for research funding, to facilitate research-based engagement and impact work with non-academic communities, and to enable the introduction and dissemination of new educational practice. The successful candidate will get involved in the development of our research community in Comparative Politics, including its connections with other Durham departments and other institutions, and innovative educational practice to enhance the learning experience of both undergraduate and postgraduate students, including PhD candidates. Among other EDI initiatives, the department is currently in the process of diversifying its curriculum, and this is a project we would be keen on the post-holder to contribute to. For more information, please visit our department pages at www.dur.ac.uk/sgia/

Strong interest in politics – The role requires a real interest in the UK’s changing political climate and desire to gain a deep knowledge of parliamentary procedure Flexibility – The role includes regular early starts and will require flexibility in working hours, including periodic short work on a Sunday. Excellent IT skills – Successful candidates will be able to touch-type and be adept at using a range of standard software Teamwork skills – The role includes producing work in a collaborative manner, and successful candidates will need good communication skills with both the team and clients Benefits 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays Health Insurance including dental and eyesight cover Access to free mental health support services Comprehensive home office set up including furniture and full IT suite Office coffee and fruit Closing Date : 28 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Successful candidates will be invited to take part in a monitoring test and interview. item.title: Research Fellow
item.description: Tax Justice UK (TJUK) is a leading campaigning organisation dedicated to transforming the UK economy and society by advocating for a fairer, more progressive, and more effective tax system. We have a track record of securing campaign wins and have successfully moved the dial on key tax justice issues such as taxes on wealth vs work. We have built strong relationships with parliamentarians, policy makers and a network of influential think tanks and organisations. We also have excellent relationships with many influential media outlets, regularly securing extensive media coverage on tax justice issues. However, we recognise we must do more to ground our work in the lives of everyday people. This is where the Research Fellow can help. Are you a qualitative researcher passionate about economic justice and community-driven research? As a Research Fellow, you will assist in fieldwork for an ambitious UK-wide study exploring how narratives on wealth taxation can build multi-ethnic class solidarity and counter division. Working directly with grassroots partners across the country, you will build relationships with local groups and co-design a community researcher model to ensure the project is deeply rooted in the places we study. Your work will focus on listening to how everyday people experience economic insecurity, understand local divisions, and respond to messaging on taxing the super-rich. This role offers a unique opportunity to gather the foundational, on-the-ground insights that will shape national narrative strategies to change tax policy. We’re looking for someone starting in their research career, who is eager to learn. We welcome applicants from all different backgrounds who have demonstrable interest in working class issues and a commitment to a fairer tax system in the UK. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Know everything about the role here https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NruW9Pos6C34WpNVVuO2UGaMGLlCU6Ii/ Closing Date : 14 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will take place on Friday, 25 September (in person in Vauxhall - we can cover any reasonable travel expenses). Please let us know as part of your application if you need any reasonable adjustments to allow you to attend the interview Application Details We are genuinely open-minded about your background and encourage people from different backgrounds and experiences to join our team. We conduct anonymous shortlisting to help promote diversity and fairness. This means we ask applicants to create an application ID (two letters and two numbers) to use instead of your name, and that you remove any reference to your name (email address, linkedin, social media) from your CV. Assessors will receive information on candidates after shortlisting. Please apply here https://forms.gle/3nKdXHCF6UCURxzt8 by 9am Website : http://taxjustice.uk

item.title: Account Executive
item.description: Meeting Place is an integrated communications agency that specialises in the built environment. We deliver planning communications and public relations campaigns to create positive change from new developments. The role: Meeting Place has an exciting opportunity for someone who wants to make a difference. There’s consensus that our country needs more homes, new space for businesses and better infrastructure. We’re looking for someone to join us and be part of the solution. You will help to create communications and engagement strategies for our clients, undertake community and political background research, develop engaging print and digital content, take part in community and stakeholder engagement events, and provide insightful reporting. You will also play an active role in supporting business development activities for Meeting Place. Who we’re looking for: We’re growing and ambitious and looking for someone who wants to grow and be ambitious with us. You might already be working in a public relation or communications role and are looking for a new challenge that aligns more with your aspirations and values. Or maybe you have valuable transferable skills from a role in client relations, political research, public affairs, or the property sector. We want to hear from you if you think you can demonstrate these to a high standard: • Excellent communication skills – you can actively listen and confidently and clearly communicate with colleagues, clients, politicians, and community stakeholders. • Collaborative spirit – you’ll enjoy working closely with colleagues, across the business and as part of our clients’ project teams. • Analytical thinking and problem solving – you feel confident undertaking research, interpreting information to make informed judgements. • Project management – you can manage your time effectively, are organised and demonstrate an eye for detail. • Enthusiasm and adaptability – you enjoy taking on new challenges and getting to grips with new projects and can adapt to changing client needs and project priorities. You should have some knowledge of or an interest in politics, the built environment, and/or the community and social impact issues that interact with the planning process. Closing Date : 4 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will be held in as soon as possible (we may appoint before the closing date) Application Details To apply send us an email along with a CV and covering letter to graceweiner@meeting-place.uk. For more information, please visit - https://meeting-place.uk/careers/account-executive-3/ Website : http://meeting-place.uk/
