item.title: Associate Director, Public Affairs
item.description: Sanctuary is an independent strategic advisory firm helping leaders and organisations build influence and shape reputation at critical moments. With colleagues from government, communications consultancies and in-house roles, we advise business leaders, governments, non-profits and individuals on building, enhancing and protecting reputations in the political sphere. Beyond political expertise, we are generalists across corporate communications and reputation management, built on long-standing client relationships, straight-talking counsel and hands-on delivery. Core Responsibilities ⁘ Leads operational running of client teams as senior delivery link with Directors and Partners; deputises for them as appropriate. ⁘ Builds trusted relationships with clients and external stakeholders, giving sound advice on political, regulatory and reputational issues. ⁘ Tracks current affairs and the political and business landscape, anticipating risks, spotting opportunities, and positioning teams for success. ⁘ Invests in developing direct reports and colleagues, coaching teams on effective delivery and senior stakeholder management. ⁘ Supports business growth: contributes to new business strategy, leads proposals, and networks to bring in new client leads. Key Skills & Experience ⁘ Proven experience in public affairs or policy, gained in agencies, corporates, trade associations, government or political parties. ⁘ Strong knowledge of the political landscape and policy process, responding reactively to events while proactively spotting opportunities for clients. ⁘ Confidently juggles multiple clients and workstreams, structuring teams and timelines, delegating and prioritising to meet deadlines. ⁘ Understands and interrogates a brief, thinks strategically, solves problems, and delivers succinct advice and senior counsel. ⁘ A clear, confident communicator verbally and in writing, drafting content and executing multistakeholder communications strategies. ⁘ Excellent interpersonal and people-management skills, guiding junior colleagues to deliver high-quality work, independently and as a team. ⁘ Professional, flexible and proactive, and enjoys contributing to building Sanctuary as a business. ⁘ Able to convince clients, senior management and teams to adopt ideas and approaches. item.title: Digital Video Producer and Editor
item.description: The Good Growth Foundation is looking for someone to help us tell the story online of what makes good growth and how we can achieve this mission across the UK. We are looking for someone who loves a TikTok trend, has cracking ideas that could form the next viral phenomenon, top notch production and editing skills and a comprehensive understanding of how digital platforms can help us make noise and campaign for good growth across the country. We’re a team full of energy and enthusiasm looking to make a big impact - want to come and help? About the Good Growth Foundation The Good Growth Foundation (GGF) is an independent political think tank on a mission to shape the future of our economy. We believe that opportunity is the key to a thriving economy, and we’re here to challenge the status quo. Using polling, focus groups, policy research and economic analysis, we develop solutions that are politically popular while pushing for growth that reduces inequality. Every individual, community, and region should have a chance to contribute. We campaign for a fairer economy, so growth can work for good. What you’ll be doing You'll be working closely with the Director of Comms to plan and produce video content across all of our platforms, helping us amplify our work and create engaging campaigns on a range of topics. You will plan, script, direct, edit and publish a variety of digital content. We're looking for someone who: Is politically switched on and social-media savvy, who understands how to communicate our innovative research to political and public digital audiences. Sees opportunities in digital content and has creative ideas about how to amplify our campaigns. Has great organisation and attention to detail. Is skilled with all software you might use, including AI-assisted editing tools. Experience in politics, campaigning, or a fast-moving startup environment is a plus - but attitude and energy matter more than a perfect CV. item.title: Research Associate 'Watts Right' Project
item.description: Based at University of York campus (with some remote working options available) The ‘Watts Right?’ Project is a collaboration between the School of Business and Society and the Department of Environment and Geography to explore the shifting nature of public sentiment on Net Zero and clean energy policy. The politics of net zero and clean energy in the UK has changed. The cross-party consensus on climate action broke down in 2025 and political positions on Net Zero have polarised. At York, Dr Stephen Hall (SBS/DEG) is leading the ‘Watts Right?’ project along with Prof Carolyn Snell (SBS). The project is an academic investigation into how members of the voting public, specifically on the political right, are experiencing net zero, clean energy, and climate policies in their lives. The project asks who has been left behind in climate policy to date, and how the framing of clean energy policy intersects with the daily lives of right of centre voters. Watts Right is funded by the UK Energy Research Centre (UKERC) and is delivered in collaboration with the University of Leeds. The successful candidate will be joining a wider group of energy researchers in the UK tackling live challenges in the energy transition. Role We are looking for an outstanding researcher to deliver an exciting series of both qualitative and quantitative engagements designed to better understand the experiences, opinions and expectations of clean energy amongst people who are currently considering voting for right of centre political parties in the UK. The successful candidate will conduct research on the Watts Right? project under the supervision of Hall and Snell and will contribute to the production of research outputs. The role includes recruiting participants to longitudinal qualitative research, which will include: developing photographic diaries, undertaking deep semi-structured interviews, and analysing political and policy attitudes to energy and climate action. The successful applicant will be able to work effectively across a diverse range of political and social contexts. Skills, Experience & Qualification needed The essential requirements for this role include an undergraduate degree alongside a PhD (close to completion or equivalent experience) in energy or climate politics, policy, or public engagement. Candidates should possess knowledge of climate/energy politics, public opinion, and public-facing qualitative research techniques, complemented by strong written and oral communication skills for publishing research, presenting at conferences, drafting proposals, and securing funding. Essential experience includes delivering independent and collaborative research, publishing academic work, and demonstrating personal attributes such as attention to detail, a collaborative and proactive ethos, strong workload prioritisation, and enthusiasm for the project's focus. Desirable assets include knowledge of domestic clean energy policy and experimental survey design, as well as practical experience in participant recruitment, ethical data management, public engagement in climate initiatives, and innovative qualitative methods centred on lived experience. Interview date: To be confirmed For informal enquiries: please contact Dr Steve Hall: steve.hall@york.ac.uk The University strives to be diverse and inclusive – a place where we can ALL be ourselves. We particularly encourage applications from people who identify as Black, Asian or from a Minority Ethnic background, who are underrepresented at the University. We offer family friendly, flexible working arrangements, with forums and inclusive facilities to support our staff. #EqualityatYork

item.title: Research Fellow
item.description: Full Time Fixed Term for 2 years We are delighted to welcome applications for the position of Research Fellow within a new ESRC-funded research project led by Prof Elizabeth Evans and Dr Stefanie Reher (Strathclyde) on Disability and Political Parties in Europe (DISPOP). Despite reporting high levels of interest in electoral politics, disabled people have lower voter turnout rates and are under-represented in legislatures around the world. To understand why these patterns occur, what barriers exist, and how to redress these inequalities, we need to study the relationship between disability and political parties - the key institution linking citizens and electoral politics. Political parties are important vehicles for mobilising and organising groups of citizens with an interest in politics; yet there are no studies focused on how disabled people experience and perceive political parties, nor whether, when, and how parties think about disability, accessibility and inclusion. DISPOP aims to: identify, analyse, and compare barriers experienced by disabled people, map and evaluate existing party initiatives and best practices, explore to what extent formal rules and informal norms render parties ableist institutions, and co-produce recommendations with disabled people to make politics more accessible. The post holder will take a prominent role in developing the conceptual and methodological innovations to study disability and political parties across four cases: Denmark, Germany, Spain and the UK. The role will require using qualitative and mixed methods, for instance; interviews, focus groups, and ethnographic methods. It may also include quantitative data analysis. The post-holder will take a role in all stages of this process, from conceptualisation to data collection and analysis, as well as writing up and presenting the findings. As such, there is scope for the post-holder to bring their own skills and interests to influence the study design. This research position will be based in the Department of Politics and International Relations within the Faculty of Social Sciences, at the University of Southampton, and the work will be carried out under the supervision of Elizabeth Evans. You will join a vibrant and growing Department with a concentration of scholars researching related themes in the Public Opinion Research Network and the Gender and Inequalities Centre. To be successful you will have completed your PhD in a relevant discipline before May 2026 (or equivalent professional qualifications). You will have: a demonstrated interest in mixed methods approach to researching political attitudes of the public and/or other key political actors and/or political parties; a facility for solving conceptual and methodological problems; the ability to plan and organise work independently and as part of a team; the ability to write research presentations and papers for peer review publication; the ability to conduct research in either Danish or Spanish is essential. Knowledge and experience of focus groups, cognitive interviewing and/or ethnographic methods is desirable. Qualitative skills are essential but experience of using mixed methods would be ideal. The Research Fellow post is full-time for a fixed term of 2 years with an anticipated start date of October 2026. The University of Southampton holds an Athena SWAN Silver Award demonstrating commitment to equal opportunities in the workplace. Informal enquiries may be addressed to Elizabeth Evans, e.j.evans@soton.ac.uk Further details:

item.title: Post-doctoral Research Associate DISPOP
item.description: The Department of Government and Public Policy invites applications from emerging scholars for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to support and contribute to the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) Responsive Mode project Disability and Political Parties (DISPOP). DISPOP is a collaborative project led by Professor Elizabeth Evans (University of Southampton) and Professor Stefanie Reher (University of Strathclyde). Despite reporting high levels of interest in electoral politics, disabled people are under-represented in legislatures around the world. To understand why these patterns occur, what barriers exist, and how to redress these inequalities, we need to study the relationship between disability and political parties - the key institution linking citizens and electoral politics. Political parties are important vehicles for mobilising and organising groups of citizens with an interest in politics; yet there are no studies focussed on how disabled people experience and perceive political parties, nor whether, when, and how parties think about disability, accessibility and inclusion. DISPOP aims to: (1) identify, analyse, and compare barriers experienced by disabled people (2) map and evaluate existing party initiatives and best practices (3) explore to what extent formal rules and informal norms render parties ableist institutions 4) co-produce recommendations with Disabled People’s Organisations to make politics more accessible. The University of Strathclyde is a leading, multi award-winning technological university in the heart of Glasgow, one of the UK’s most exciting student cities. Rated by the Daily Mail as University of the Year 2026, research is central to everything we do. It informs our teaching and helps us make a difference to business, industry and society. Almost 90% of research produced by the University of Strathclyde was rated ‘world-leading’ or ‘internationally excellent’ in the UK Research Excellence Framework (REF) 2021. The Department of Government and Public Policy combines world-class teaching and research exploring political systems and institutions worldwide. The Department has particular strength in the study of political representation of under-represented groups and quantitative methods. Our Research Excellence Framework 2021 submission was the highest-rated in the UK, with 62% of research rated world-leading and 100% of impact rated outstanding. The post holder will play a prominent role in developing conceptual and methodological innovations to study disability and political parties across Denmark, Germany, Spain and the UK. The role will require using quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods, including survey design and analysis, survey experiments, interviews, and ethnographic methods. The post holder will take a role in all stages of the research process, from conceptualisation to data collection and analysis, as well as writing up and presenting findings, including attending international and domestic conferences and co-authoring publications. There is scope for the post holder to bring their own skills and interests to the study design. The post holder will work under the supervision of Professor Stefanie Reher and in close collaboration with Professor Elizabeth Evans and a postdoctoral research associate at the University of Southampton. The post holder will be the main point of contact for either the Danish or Spanish case. Therefore, it is a strong advantage for applicants to be familiar with the political party system in either Denmark or Spain, and have good writing and conversation skills in either Danish or Spanish, in addition to having a keen interest in the role of disability in politics.

item.title: Comparative Data & Methods Postdoctoral Researcher
item.description: Oxford Department of International Development, Queen Elizabeth House, 3 Mansfield Road, Oxford, OX1 3TB The Oxford Department of International Development (ODID) is seeking to recruit a Comparative Data & Methods Postdoctoral Researcher. Reporting to Professor Masooda Bano, the post-holder will join a research team funded by a European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant, Choosing Islamic Conservatism: Muslim Youth in Europe and the UK and the Question of Social Cohesion. Building on the earlier phases of the project, the team is now establishing the European Muslim Observatory: Comparative Research Infrastructure on Muslim Institutional Development in Europe. The Observatory aims to develop the first systematic comparative research infrastructure documenting the institutional development of Islam and Muslim communities across Europe. It will bring together legal, political, institutional and religious data to examine how Muslim institutions evolve in interaction with constitutional frameworks, state institutions and wider society, creating a lasting research resource for comparative scholarship on Islam in Europe. The Observatory aims to establish a lasting comparative database that will support future academic research, policy engagement and international collaboration beyond the lifetime of the current ERC grant. Successful applicants will become part of the founding research team responsible for designing, developing and implementing this new research infrastructure. This post is offered for 18 months. The successful candidate will have ( or will be near to completion) a PhD in Political Science, Comparative Politics, Sociology, Public Policy, Development Studies or a closely related discipline. They will also have demonstrated experience working on comparative research projects. Experience working with comparative datasets or research databases is essential to this role. At ODID we embrace and cherish our differences, and endeavour to be considerate and welcoming of all. You are most welcome at ODID, without the need to hide any part of who you are. We acknowledge societal inequalities and how these affect us, and those around us, personally and professionally. We hold an Athena Swan bronze award in recognition of our efforts to introduce organisational and cultural changes which promote equality, cherish diversity and create a better working environment for all. We are also taking active steps to promote race equality and reduce the risk of bias and discrimination. We work together to enrich, fortify and grow our community and dedicate our combined efforts to teaching and research to increase our impact and influence in development debates at the national and global level. We encourage all eligible candidates to apply for our vacancies and join us in pursuing our goals. Applications for this vacancy are to be made online. You will be required to upload a CV and supporting statement as part of your online application. Please note that only the CV and supporting statement will be considered; any other documents uploaded will not be reviewed as part of the shortlisting process. Only applications received before 12 midday on Thursday, 24 September 2026 can be considered.

item.title: Administrative Assistant - Part Time
item.description: The Administrative Assistant will help the MP and office run smoothly. The role will involve managing the office budget, supporting the MP's diary, looking after office arrangements, organising meetings and events, helping with correspondence and ensuring the office follows Parliamentary rules and procedures. The role will work across both the Westminster and constituency offices, and is part-time for 3 days a week (21 hours per week either as 3 full days or spread out over 5 days). Key Duties & Responsibilities Finance, Budget & Compliance Budget management: Help manage the office budget and make sure spending follows IPSA rules. Expenses & payroll: Submit expense claims through IPSA Online, help manage staff payroll and keep accurate financial records. Data protection: Help ensure that constituent information is handled securely and confidentially, in line with GDPR and Parliamentary requirements. Diary & Executive Support Diary management: Help manage the MP's busy diary, balancing Parliamentary commitments such as debates and votes with constituency meetings, surgeries, visits and events. Administrative support: Help with correspondence, briefings, travel arrangements and other tasks for the MP as required. Meetings & events: Organise the practical arrangements for surgeries, meetings and public events, including venues, guest lists, suppliers and on-the-day support. Office & Operations Office management: Help manage the Westminster and constituency offices, including IT, health and safety, security and general office arrangements. Suppliers: Manage relationships with suppliers for office equipment, supplies, maintenance and other services. Projects: Help deliver projects that improve how the office works and the service provided to constituents. Communications & Correspondence Inbox management: Help organise and manage the office inbox, ensuring correspondence is dealt with efficiently and passed to the right member of staff. Correspondence: Help prepare and send responses to constituents and other correspondence as required. Working Conditions Part-time (21 hours per week either as 3 full days or spread out over 5 days), with occasional requirements to work outside normal office hours and travel between the Westminster and constituency offices as operational needs dictate. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 11 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Application Details Please send a CV and covering letter to liam.conlon.mp@parliament.uk . Please direct any queries or questions to the same address. Website : http://liamconlon.com/

item.title: Project Support Manager
item.description: About Spacehive Spacehive is a tech-for-good company on a mission to make it easy for people to improve their local area. Working in partnership with local authorities, our platform helps groups and individuals design and fund ideas that bring places to life, from phone boxes turned into community libraries and pop-up gardens, to street art and community solar. We have the highest success rate of any UK crowdfunding platform, and over £44 million has been raised on it. Our users, and their imaginative ideas, are the magic at the heart of our business. About the role We're looking for a Project Support Manager who's passionate about community empowerment and exceptional customer service. You'll be the first port of call for our project creators and their backers on our platform. We're proud that 98% of our user interactions are rated good or excellent, and this role is key to that. What you'll do Offer expert crowdfunding advice (we'll brief you), helping people plan and run campaigns Communicate with users by email and phone, clearly and warmly Review and improve the support function and internal operations Maintain our Help Centre, creating guides and video tutorials Support the delivery of online workshops for project creators Investigate, resolve, escalate and report user issues Feed user insights to the product team and roadmap About you An eager learner who'll quickly become a Spacehive crowdfunding expert Exceptional interpersonal skills: empathy, politeness and patience Able to turn user feedback into platform improvements Strong organisation, time management and prioritisation A confident yet humble team player who'll get stuck in Driven and proactive, working to exceed targets We don't need years of experience, just a real passion for great service and empathy with our diverse users. The role is fully remote, 4 days a week; we don't require fixed days or have core working hours. We welcome applicants who require flexibility. Spacehive is an anti-racist, anti-discriminatory organisation. We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic people, people with disabilities, and people from lower income and diverse educational backgrounds who may be under-represented in our organisation. Combining political insight with strategic communications expertise, we deliver clear advice, practical solutions and tangible outcomes. As a small, hands-on team, interns work alongside our consultants from day one, contributing directly to live client projects. item.title: Caseworker
item.description: This position is advertised within the remit of the Westminster office or the constituency office, depending on the candidate. As a Caseworker in the office of Terry Jermy MP, you will be part of a dedicated team committed to supporting constituents with a wide range of issues. Working alongside our team of Caseworkers, your role will involve handling casework empathetically and efficiently, liaising with government departments and local agencies, and ensuring timely and appropriate responses to constituent concerns. You will maintain accurate records, draft correspondence, and contribute to the smooth running of the MP’s office, helping to make a meaningful difference in the lives of local residents. Depending on the candidate, this role may be based in Westminster or the South West Norfolk constituency. Experience in casework is preferred, however experience in a similar role providing advice to individuals will be considered. The position requires excellent communication skills, the ability to collaborate and build relationships, and strong administrative and organisational skills to manage a busy workload. Key Responsibilities • Critically analyse patterns of enquiries and articulate the findings in reports and communication with the MP and other staff members • Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as assisting on more complex cases from members of the public by phone, email, social media, or face-to-face. Ongoing communication may be required • Draft responses to constituents • Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially in line with the data protection legislation • Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially, and accurately in accordance with the MP • Gather relevant information to assist with resolving cases • Log all cases; monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken • Retain records and information confidentially and in line with the Data Protection Act • Assist with preparing and attending surgeries and other meetings and follow up as appropriate • There may be a requirement for the role holder to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for work occasionally Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 28 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Start Date: ASAP upon appointment. You will be required to undergo security clearance before commencing employment. If invited to interview you will be required to complete a written exercise as well as a panel-style interview. Application Details To apply, please send a CV (no more than two sides) and a Cover Letter (no more than one side) to the Constituency Office Manager, Liz Bernard, liz.bernard@parliament.uk with the subject line 'Caseworker Application'. Website : http://terryjermy.com

Job Description Oversee and manage the small casework team to ensure target response times are met Handle correspondence from constituents, drafting responses and providing advice and support to constituents on a variety of issues (e.g. housing, immigration, benefits) through liaison with Government agencies, the voluntary sector and others. Manage own caseload and progress of casework, ensuring all cases are dealt with in a sensitive, confidential and timely manner and accurate records are kept in adherence to the principles of the Data Protection Act and GDPR. Attend surgeries and other meetings to assist the Member in dealing with constituents’ issues. Research and draft responses or respond to constituents on any issues raised on behalf of the Member. Liaise with relevant groups within the constituency and communicate appropriately with internal and external contacts. Person Specification Previous experience of handling casework, either in an MP’s Office, the Civil Service, or a third sector organisation such as the CAB is essential. Previous experience of supervising colleagues in a small team is highly desirable Excellent verbal and written communication skills and confidence in interacting with people at all levels and in a variety of circumstances. Able to prioritise a demanding workload to meet deadlines. Able to deal with issues in a confidential manner. Able to work effectively in a small team. Competent use of IT including full proficiency in Microsoft Office, Outlook and the internet. Experience of a casework management system or similar database would be an advantage. Experience of working and dealing with the general public. Awareness and understanding of current political issues. Sympathetic to the aims and objectives of the Labour Party. item.title: Professor and Head of Department of Politics and Public Administration
item.description: Applications are invited for appointment as Professor and Head of the Department of Politics and Public Administration, Faculty of Social Sciences at The University of Hong Kong (Ref.: 537112). We are seeking a distinguished scholar with the stature of a Full Professor at a research-intensive institution, a strong record of academic leadership, and a solid commitment to research, teaching, and community engagement to lead our world-class department. Candidates should hold a PhD in Political Science or related discipline. The appointment as Professor will be made on tenure terms, while the appointment as Head of Department will be for an initial three-year term, renewable subject to mutual agreement. Department of Politics and Public Administration The Department of Politics and Public Administration has played a leading role in the University and its global disciplines since its establishment in 1970. In addition to a competitive PhD research degree programme, the Department offers three highly successful taught postgraduate programmes – Master of Public Administration (MPA), Master in International and Public Affairs (MIPA), and Doctor of Public Administration (DPA) – as well as thriving undergraduate programmes. The Department’s faculty members are research active, diverse, international and highly collegial. Many have received training and work experience in the most prestigious departments and universities in North America, Europe and across Asia. Their expertise spans the fields of Comparative Politics, International Relations, Political Theory, and Public Administration. For more information about the Department, visit https://ppa.hku.hk/ . Position Description The Department is looking for a visionary leader who will be responsible for both strategic and operational leadership within the Department, and contribute a significant voice in the leadership structure of the Faculty. Through effective leadership and coordination, he/she will champion the activities of the Department and will seek to align them with the Faculty’s strategic research areas. We seek a scholar of the highest academic credentials who has a commitment to helping build a community of scholars. The area of research expertise is open, but the appointee should have the experience and capability required to lead the Department. The appointee will lead strategic planning within the Department to deliver positive outcomes across our research and teaching programmes. He/She will bring experience in leadership and administration, and strong interpersonal skills to the role. Compensation and Benefits A highly competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and experience will be offered, in addition to annual leave and medical benefits. The University will contribute up to 15% of basis salary into the retirement benefits scheme. At current rates, salaries tax does not exceed 15% of gross income. Housing benefits will be provided as applicable. Application The University only accepts online application for the above post. Applicants should apply online at the University’s career site by clicking the 'Apply' button and upload (1) an up-to-date C.V. with contact information of three referees, (2) a cover letter, (3) a research plan, (4) a statement on teaching philosophy, and (5) an outline of the vision and mission as Head of Department. Review of applications will commence as soon as possible and continue until November 15, 2026 , or until the post is filled, whichever is earlier. The University is an equal opportunities employer and is committed to equality, ethics, inclusivity, diversity and transparency

item.title: Head of Campaigns
item.description: JOIN OUR TEAM! This is an exciting opportunity to join The End Violence Against Women Coalition (EVAW) as our Head of Campaigns to lead on our campaigns work to end violence against women and girls in all its forms. The last few years have seen a huge increase in awareness of violence against women and girls, and support for our work. With this crucial human rights issue on the public and political agenda like never before, now is the time to disrupt the status quo and lay the foundations for a different world. ABOUT THE ROLE This is an exciting new role that will see the postholder leading EVAW’s strategic, influential campaigns work. The postholder will drive EVAW’s planned and reactive campaigning, advising the Director(s) and working closely with Heads of Communications, Policy and Research, Public Affairs and Membership functions within the organisation. The role is frontfacing, requiring the postholder to confidently represent the organisation in high-level stakeholder spaces, as well as in the media. The postholder will lead on monitoring, evaluation and learning, ensuring the efficacy of our campaigns and interventions, as well as promoting internal learning and reflection. Using their strong campaigning nous/instinct the postholder will also be effective at adapting or amending campaigns and interventions when the external landscape shifts. The postholder will have a finger on the pulse of current affairs and trends, and be willing and able balance reactive and responsive work with delivering planned outputs and activities. You should be comfortable both working at pace, and with taking time to reflect and re-strategise. You are likely to have experience in campaigns, working on VAWG or another human rights/equalities issue, and will be seeking an opportunity to work in a highly impactful, agile and dynamic feminist organisation. Whether practical or academic, paid or voluntary, a background in VAWG will of course be an asset. You’ll need to show you have a good understanding of VAWG, can communicate complex issues with clarity and impact, and are committed to intersectional feminism. The applications which stand out in this process will be from those who deeply believe in what we do. Closing Date : 21 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Applications must be received by 5pm. Shortlisted candidates will be notified by the week commencing 12 October 2026 and interviews will take place in London on the 20th, 22nd, and 23rd October 2026. Start date TBC Application Details Apply via the End Violence Against Women Coalition website: https://www.endviolenceagainstwomen.org.uk/head-of-campaigns/ You will be asked to submit a CV, complete an application form and complete an equality and diversity monitoring form. Download the job description: https://www.endviolenceagainstwomen.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Head-of-Campaigns-JD-2026.pdf Website : http://www.endviolenceagainstwomen.org.uk/

The ideal candidate will have: • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with a range of audiences. • Strong experience in media, social media and/or digital communications. • Strong digital content creation and delivery skills. • An understanding of digital media trends, political communications and campaigning. • Excellent research, analytical and problem-solving skills. • The ability to identify opportunities, develop creative ideas and turn them into effective communications and campaigns. • Strong organisational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage and prioritise a demanding workload. • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to meet tight deadlines. item.title: Political and Legislative Adviser
item.description: The Leader and Chief Whip of the Opposition in the House of Lords are looking for a researcher to join an existing team that supports them and their wider frontbench in scrutinising the Government's business and legislative programme. This is an excellent opportunity to be part of a supportive and dedicated team working at the heart of Westminster, effecting real change through the legislative process. Responsibilities: Including but not limited to - Conducting research and producing briefings on legislative matters, policy issues and current affairs. Drafting questions, speeches and amendments to legislation in consultation with our frontbench. Assisting the wider team with other duties that may be specified from time to time by the Leader or Chief Whip of the Opposition, their Chief of Staff or Deputy Chief of Staff. Skills/Experience: We are looking for someone with a strong work ethic who take pride in carrying out their work honestly, reliably and diligently to the best of their ability. Applicants should have the following skills and attributes - Legal, Parliamentary and Policy Knowledge: familiarity with, and interest in, legislation, parliament, policy, current affairs and the political landscape. Research Skills: ability to analyse and summarise complex information from various sources in to clear and concise written briefings. Writing Skills: ability to write accurate and coherent briefings and speeches on a range of topics, often to tight deadlines. Confidentiality: the upmost integrity, trustworthiness and discretion. Adaptability: willingness to handle unexpected changes or urgent request and work flexibly as part of a wider team. The successsful applicant is likley to cover an MHCLG and DHSC desks. Knowledge or expereince in these areas is prefered but not essential. Other Information: Candidates should be sympathetic to aims of the Conservative Party. This role is fixed-term until 31st March 2027, with the possibility of extension. Key responsibilities • Research, draft and send high-quality responses to constituent policy queries • Lead the policy and campaigns process for the office, overseeing master drafts and version control, to support a timely and efficient sign off procedure • Work closely with the wider team to ensure residents are regularly updated on the work of the MP in the constituency and in Westminster • Critically analyse patterns of enquiries and articulate the findings in reports and communication with the MP and other staff members • Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as assisting on more complex cases from members of the public by phone, email, social media or face to face • Draft responses to constituents • Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially in line with data protection legislation • Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately in accordance with the MP • Gather relevant information to assist with resolving cases • Log all cases; monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken • Ensure all enquiries are dealt with in a timely manner • There may be a requirement for the role holder to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for work occasionally • Sympathetic to the aims, values and objectives of the Labour Party Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 9 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Closing time: 5pm Interviews: Week beginning 14th September 2026 Start date: To be agreed and based on notice period Due to the high volume of expected applications we are only able to contact you if you have been shortlisted. Thank you. item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: Tom Rutland MP is seeking to recruit a Communications Officer to join his team on a full-time basis, to support him with his work on behalf of the constituents of East Worthing & Shoreham. This is an ideal opportunity to support an active & engaged MP, where you will be involved in all areas of Tom's work, with opportunity to contribute & work collaboratively. The role includes the management and drafting of responses to policy enquiries, developing effective communication strategies, producing content for social media and media outlets, and working on projects and campaigns to support the MP’s work in the constituency. Duties will include: • Researching and drafting responses to constituents on policy and campaign issues • Producing written copy for media outlets and responding to press queries • Monitoring media coverage and social media channels • Producing graphical and video content for social media • Supporting wider communications objectives via mass mailing • Establishing effective working relationships with local stakeholders • Undertaking research to ensure MP is accurately informed on key issues affecting relevant interests • Horizon scanning to identify opportunities to pursue topics of local importance & to progress priority campaigns Person specification (Essential) • Exceptional written & verbal communication skills & the ability to produce high-quality copy. • An interest in current affairs & policy issues. • Ability to build relationships with a range of stakeholders. • Knowledge of how to use social media, websites & email. • Understanding of how to produce graphics and video content. • Experience of researching & presenting information in an easily digestible format • Ability to work well as part of a team • Ability to use own initiative • Ability to work well under pressure, multi-task & able to meet tight deadlines • Commitment to the values of the Labour Party Desirable • Previous experience working in Parliament or with MPs • Knowledge of how to analyse online metrics to improve future communications • Experience of using Adobe and Canva • Good all-round IT skills There may be a requirement for the role holder to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for work occasionally. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 1 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will take place in the week commencing Monday 7th September, with online interviews being a possibility. Shortlisted applicants will be contacted by the end of Friday 4th September. We will ideally be looking for someone to start by the end of October 2026. Application Details Candidates should send their CV (no more than 2 pages) and covering letter (no more than one page) outlining their suitability for the role. Please send your email to helen.mackie@parliament.uk with the subject line “Communications Officer application – First Name Last Name”. Website : http://tom4ewas.co.uk

item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: Shivani Raja MP is looking for a proactive and creative Communications Officer to join her Leicester East constituency team. This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to build hands-on experience shaping how an MP communicates with, and is held accountable to, the community she represents. You'll take the lead on Shivani's social media and online presence, produce graphics and video content, draft press releases, and help analyse casework trends so the office can better understand and respond to what Leicester East residents are raising with us. Key Responsibilities Establish, monitor and update Shivani's social media and online presence in the constituency, including producing graphics and video content and publicising surgeries and news alerts. Manage and monitor social media enquiries, dealing with cases that don't need to be transferred to a higher level, and ensuring all enquiries are handled in a timely manner. Monitor media coverage, liaise with the media, and prepare press releases on constituency, non-party-political matters. Analyse patterns of enquiries and produce reports, articulating findings clearly to the MP and other staff members. Assist with surgeries and other meetings, following up as appropriate, and attend constituency meetings as required. Support with drafting responses to constituents and handling more complex cases by phone, email, social media or face to face. Log cases, monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken, keeping records confidentially and in line with data protection legislation. Any other reasonable management request. There may be a requirement to work outside normal working hours and to travel for work occasionally. Who We're Looking For We welcome applicants who are creative, organised and confident communicators, with a good eye for content and a solid understanding of how social media platforms work in practice. Attention to detail, discretion in handling confidential information, and good political judgement are all essential. Experience with design or video editing tools is desirable but not required; what matters most is a strong instinct for what will land with a Leicester East audience. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 18 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, so early submissions are encouraged. Interviews will take place as soon as possible with a start date as soon as possible thereafter. Application Details Please send your CV and a covering letter as a PDF to: Shivani.Raja.MP@Parliament.uk (Subject line: "Communications Officer Application") Or by post to: Shivani Raja MP, 7 Loughborough Road, Leicester, LE4 5LJ (Marked "Communications Officer Application") Website : https://www.shivaniraja.uk/

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Location: Remote with significant UK-based activity such as DfE and sector engagement. The CEO will be responsible for the overall leadership, performance and sustainability of CES. Working with the Board of Trustees and senior executive team, they will: execute against the organisation’s strategy and mission, oversee its programme of research, policy engagement and impact, ensure effective financial and operational management, sustain regular income through fundraising. Key responsibilities Lead a matrix structure that can include the core executive team as well as temporary research associates, assistants and academic partners. Secure and diversify income through fundraising, partnerships, and grant applications. Work with the CRO to oversee CES’s research portfolio. Nurture relationships with ministers and civil servants, other education research organisations, funders or potential funders, and the wider policy ecosystem. Act as spokesperson for CES in the media. Maintain strong financial oversight, including budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting and accountability to trustees and funders. Person specification Essential Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex research and policy issues clearly to different audiences. An understanding of how education policy is developed in the UK. Proven people-management experience, a willingness to deal with a matrix personnel structure and able to accommodate contractors and partners with other commitments. Experience with fundraising for a charitable or not-for-profit organisation, or a willingness to upskill in this area. Experience of managing budgets and interpreting financial information. Desirable Experience of policy stakeholder engagement or public affairs. An understanding of research practices and methodologies, particularly in relation to public policy analysis and comparative case study methods. An established and relevant network of contacts across the UK education ecosystem. Experience of leading a research, policy, education or charitable organisation. Closing Date : 20 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Start date: as soon as possible Application Details Please send a CV and a short cover letter to lisa.bowett@ces.partners , or apply via LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4457340852/ Unfortunately we will be unable to respond to unsucessful candidates. Please contact lisa.bowett@ces.partners if you would like any more information. Website : http://www.ces.partners/

item.title: Digital and Communications Officer
item.description: Peter is looking for someone who can create campaigns and drive engagement. This is a role for somebody who spots opportunities, thinks differently and brings forward fresh ideas. Working at the heart of a fast-paced operation, you will lead on digital content, social media, graphics, video production and press activity. One day you could be filming and editing content for social media, the next drafting a press release, responding to breaking news or helping deliver a major local campaign. This is an exciting opportunity for somebody who enjoys working in a fast-moving environment, thinking on their feet and taking ownership of their work. As the role will include work with Peter in the constituency it would suit someone who lives near the Bromley area. A clean driving licence and access to a car preferred. Key Responsibilities • Creating engaging graphics, video content and digital campaigns. • Managing and growing social media platforms. • Drafting press releases, statements and media briefings. • Producing content for websites, newsletters and digital communications. • Identifying opportunities for Op Eds, major newspaper articles • Monitoring media coverage and identifying opportunities to generate engagement. • Working with colleagues to promote local campaigns, events and parliamentary activity. • Supporting media relations and responding to fast-moving issues. Essential Skills & Experience • Excellent graphic design and content creation skills. • Experience using software such as Photoshop, InDesign, Premiere Pro, Canva or equivalent. • Strong video filming and editing capability. • Outstanding written communication skills. • Ability to work quickly, accurately and under pressure. • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail. • Ability to generate creative ideas and think outside the box. • Confidence working independently and as part of a small team. A keen interest in politics and current affairs is essential, as is sympathy with the aims and values of the Conservative Party. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 11 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews may be held prior to the closing date. Early applications are encouraged. Start date of early/mid October. Application Details Please submit: • A CV • A covering letter • Examples of graphics, videos or campaigns you have produced By 10pm on the closing date, to gill.lee@parliament.uk Website : https://www.peterfortune.co.uk/
